comparator.sourceNotes: The current curriculum is represented by its 45 separately credited compulsory study units totaling 150 EC, rather than ten opaque 15-EC parent labels. Genuine integrated project and academic-skills units remain intact; parents and children are never stacked. The third year preserves two generic 15-EC minor slots, Production Systems Engineering and the 12-EC research assignment plus 3-EC societal embedding.

alternatives.concept: Develop mathematical system models, algorithms, data methods and robotics alongside product design, life-cycle assessment, circular resource technology and renewable-energy analysis. This is a related-fields response; mechanical structures, thermal-fluid science, materials/manufacturing formation and engineering build-test projects remain explicit gaps.

progressionAssessment.rationale: The schedule contains 24 unique courses, 180 EC, PPD in year one and ten advanced courses. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is available in its assigned Fall 2026 cohort semester. Programming precedes algorithms and optimisation; Mathematical Methods precedes all later mathematics, robotics and neural-network work; Sustainability Essentials I precedes II, which precedes recovery, resource and renewable-system study.

alternativeSelection.assessment: One complete related-fields response passes the evidence, course-content and schedule gates. It combines mathematical system modelling, algorithms, data, robotics, product design, energy assessment, life-cycle analysis and resource technology. It is not represented as Mechanical Engineering. A separate structural/mechanical-design and manufacturing direction cannot supply statics, mechanics of materials, dynamics, elasticity, machine elements, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, heat transfer, tribology, manufacturing processes or the repeated build-and-test project sequence. A second energy-only route would reuse the existing energy strand while discarding the systems and design content that makes the accepted response coherent, so it was not included.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both introduce programming for modelling and technical problem solving; UCR supplies general Python programming rather than the external engineering-modelling sequence.
Both establish calculus foundations for quantitative engineering models; the external component belongs to a longer engineering-mathematics sequence.
Both directly study matrices, vectors and linear algebra for system representation.
Both extend calculus and differential-equation methods; UCR is general mathematical study rather than embedded mechanical analysis.
Both analyse systems through mathematical models; UCR covers linear systems, transfer functions and state-space without the full engineering context.
Both provide probability/statistics for quantitative modelling and research.

The external project analyses and redesigns integrated mechanical/mechatronic systems. Computational robot kinematics and motion planning do not establish an important part of this project's specified hardware/system-redesign work; Robotics remains complementary study.

General root-finding, interpolation, numerical integration and ordinary-differential-equation algorithms provide foundations but do not establish finite-element discretisation or finite-element analysis. No direct finite-element method is evidenced in the selected UCR course.
Both use a team design process involving requirements, prototyping and product development; UCR does not reproduce mechanical-tool design or the target’s cumulative engineering-project sequence.
Both directly evaluate environmental impacts across product or process life cycles.

Both directly analyse an energy system and assess technical choices. UCR evaluates energy use and renewable options with technical/economic analysis and a partner report; it does not reproduce the external project's material and thermodynamic engineering analysis.

notes.text: The UCR programme provides substantial mathematical, computational, robotic, product-design and sustainable-technology study.
